Subject: RE: Procurement questionnaire - SLO definitions / monitoring / dashboard access

Hi Bethany — thanks for the patience. Please find a concise answers packet below and an evidence bundle attached. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through any item.

Summary answers (high level):
- Uptime SLOs: measured as successful API availability over rolling 30-day windows by default. We report both rolling 30d and calendar month on request. The primary uptime metric is successful response rate for the Redwood inference API (2xx responses within the configured timeout).
- Latency SLOs: we report P50, P95, and P99 for inference latency. Contract SLOs typically specify P95 (typical) and P99 (high tail). Measurement uses server-side timings at egress (time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token for completions).
- Measurement buckets: metrics are calculated from sampled request telemetry. Default sampling is 100% for managed customers during onboarding, then adaptive sampling for scale. For very high-volume customers we sample according to a workload-aware policy; we preserve unbiased buckets for SLO windows to avoid biasing tail estimates.
- Monitoring & alerting: we maintain alert rules for SLO burn-rate (30m/6h/24h windows), node-level GPU health, and queueing latency. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty and can be configured per-customer. Thresholds and escalation playbooks are in the evidence packet.
- Customer dashboard & access: We offer read-only Grafana dashboards with pre-populated panels (SLOs, token counts, error breakdowns, queue depth) and a time-limited API token for exports. Link (read-only): https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/atlas-readonly?orgId=1&panelId=5. Access governance: token scoped to project, IP allowlist option available.
- Retention & evidence: raw traces retained 90 days by default; aggregated metric rolls kept 24 months. We can provide an evidence export (CSV/GZIP) for procurement audits on request.
- Temporary sampling waiver: We can support a temporary increase in sampling fidelity for GA rollouts. Standard short-term waiver: up to 14 days with no contract amendment — billing is on standard usage (higher telemetry may change ingested event counts); if Atlas requests extended elevated sampling (>14 days), we need a short addendum (we've modeled 15–30 days as a small uplift and can propose credit language).

Attachments: SLO_evidence_packet_20250916.zip (contains sample dashboards, alert rules, instrumentation notes, and a one-page measurement appendix).

Quoted excerpt from our measurement appendix (for clarity):
"SLOs are computed from request-level telemetry aggregated into minute buckets. Rolling-window calculations use the last 30*24*60 buckets; P95/P99 computation uses weighted quantile approximations to preserve stable tail estimates under sampling."

If you want the contract language for a 30-day sampling extension, we can have Contracts draft an addendum. Otherwise, 14 days is available immediately via console configuration.

Next step? Suggest we send the packet to your procurement mailbox and offer a 20-minute walkthrough.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: SLO_evidence_packet_20250916.zip - dashboards, alert rules, measurement appendix)
